jamie_support: FYI — ACME flagged embeddings endpoint returning vectors with the wrong dimension intermittently and a big billing jump. sample req_id=req_0xA12. Started ~2026-03-15 03:10 UTC. Anyone seen this?

maria_g: Can you paste the exact curl + model name and whether they're using prefixing or caching? Also any customer-side batching?

jamie_support: here's their minimal request (redacted keys):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED" \
  -d '{"model":"open-e-1024","input":["doc1","doc2"],"prefix":"acme-main"}'
```
They say sometimes vectors come back length 1536 and sometimes 1024. They claim they rotated models and used the same prefix. Billing line item shows duplicate write spikes to cache-store around the same window.

devon_m: hmm — suspicious. If client reuses a prefix across model revisions and our cache key doesn't include model_revision/quantization, we can get stale hits or mismatched dims. Is the proxy including model+quant flags in the cache key?

alyssa_sre: attaching a slice of proxy logs around req_0xA12:
```
[03:09:58] cache_get key=acme-main|hashed_user|v1 -> HIT (dim=1024)
[03:10:01] upstream req req_0xA12 -> model=open-e-1536, serving_dim=1536
[03:10:01] cache_set key=acme-main|hashed_user|v1 -> STORED (dim=1536)
```
Note: same key used for different dims — looks like key didn't include model_revision.

embed-bot: PREFETCH event: tenant=acme, prefix=acme-main, scheduled_prefetch=03:08:00, model=open-e-1024 -> prefetch wrote 8 entries

jamie_support: customer used a rolling deploy: open-e-1024 -> open-e-1536 during that time. They also had concurrent batched requests. Billing spike likely from prefetch + live writes colliding.

eng-ml-scc: Confirmed root cause hypothesis: cache key omitted model_revision and float format. Two things happened: (1) background prefetch wrote keys for old model; (2) the rollout updated model, leading to writes with new dims under same key. When read back, some clients got HITs with wrong dim. The billing duplication came from prefetch + eager recompute. Immediate mitigations:
- Turn off tenant-level prefix reuse in prefetcher (config toggle)
- Add a temporary override that appends model_name:model_rev to cache key at proxy level

maria_g: can you reproduce locally? steps to repro I used:
1) Start prefetcher writing prefix=acme-main for model=open-e-1024
2) concurrently send batches that trigger switching to open-e-1536
3) run: `seq 1 200 | xargs -P8 -I{} curl ...` with concurrency 8 and batch size 16

devon_m: for a long-term fix we should change cache key to include: tenant_id|prefix|model_name|model_revision|quant_flag|vector_dim. Also update cache TTL behavior: eviction on model rollouts. I'll open an RFC.

jamie_support: created ticket INF-7829 and added logs + customer repro. Marking this P1 for ACME. I'll ask CS to explain billing spike and offer a credit while we patch.

alyssa_sre: I'll schedule a canary patch to include model_revision in key and roll to 10% of proxy fleet. Also gating by a feature flag. ETA tomorrow 06:00 UTC.

eng-ml-scc: after canary we should run the repro for 30 minutes at ramped load. If clean, promote. Also update docs: 'embedding-prefixing' section to warn about reusing prefixes across model rollouts.

maria_g: customer follow-up draft: "We found a cache key edge case when reusing prefixes across model rollouts. We're patching the service and will credit the unexpected usage. Temporary mitigation: set unique prefix per model version or toggle prefix-prefetch in Console."

jamie_support: thanks all — next steps captured in INF-7829. cc: @support-billing to start credit review.

support-billing: acknowledged, pulling billing window and will propose credit.

jamie_support: I'll post updates in this thread during canary. :thumbsup:
